title: The canon's quotation layer
statement: The canon's Hebrew-Bible quotations are mediated through Edouard Dhorme's Pleiade translation (Gallimard, 1956/1959): the distinctive Dhorme orthography and philological choices — Iahve for the Tetragrammaton, the preserved plural Elohim, the literal operational vocabulary — are the textual layer through which The Book Which Tells the Truth cites scripture, and the canon's own account places the Dhorme Bible in Vorilhon's hands at the 1973 contact; the canon's biblical layer therefore descends from the French rationalist-philological tradition's most literal scholarly translation, a checkable textual fact with consequences for every quotation-level reading the corpus makes.

includes: The textual identification: the canon's quotations carry Dhorme's orthography and renderings, verifiable by direct comparison (the Iahve spelling in the digitized quotations as the immediate marker)
The provenance clause at the canon's own grade: the source's account of the Dhorme volume at the 1973 contact is the canon's self-report, carried as such under the woh-claim-0020 discipline

The consequence the record exists to register: quotation-level readings in the corpus (the preserved Elohim plural above all) inherit Dhorme's philological choices, and the corpus says so rather than treating the quotations as unmediated text
excludes: Any claim that Dhorme's philology endorses the framework; Dhorme's literalism is scholarly method, and the record enlists neither the translator nor his academy
Text-critical adjudication between Dhorme, the Masoretic text, and the versions — the corpus's own translation program (woh-claim-0061) does that work under its own rules
The canon's non-biblical content, which has no quotation layer to mediate

source_references.locator: The biblical quotations throughout, carrying the Dhorme orthography (verified instance: 'Iahve fit pleuvoir...' at TBWTT-WOH 2:86); the encounter narrative's Bible in chapter 1
The Pleiade Old Testament (1956/1959) as the identified quotation source: Iahve, the preserved Elohim plural, the literal operational register

alternatives.statement: The quotation layer may be mixed rather than uniform — memory quotation, paraphrase, or a second French version in places — so the Dhorme identification should be held per-quotation, not corpus-wide, until a full collation exists.
Translation mediation is universal and trivial: every modern reader of scripture reads through some version, and nothing framework-relevant follows from which one.

revision_triggers: A collation of the canon's quotations against the Pleiade text is completed, moving the identification from marker-verified to collated (or qualifying it).
Claim woh-claim-0020's handling of the contact narrative changes in a way that reaches the Dhorme-in-hand clause.
Public prose treats Dhorme's philology as endorsement of the framework, which this record excludes.
